definition: NVIDIA's open-source library for running large language models fast on NVIDIA GPUs: custom kernels plus runtime features such as continuous batching, a paged KV cache, FP8/FP4 quantization and speculative decoding.
Merging several small GPU programs (kernels) into one so intermediate results stay in on-chip memory instead of being written to and re-read from HBM. It cuts memory traffic and launch overhead.
Sending each new request to the server that already holds the largest part of its conversation or prompt in its KV cache, so less of the prompt has to be recomputed. It shortens time to first token.
Dynamo's component that stores KV-cache blocks across tiers (GPU memory, CPU memory, SSD, remote storage) and moves them back to the GPU when a conversation resumes.

NVIDIA Inference Xfer Library: open-source software that moves KV-cache blocks and other data point-to-point between GPUs, CPU memory and storage over NVLink or RDMA, used by Dynamo for disaggregated serving.

Tokens an AI system generates each second for every megawatt of power it draws, usually at a stated speed per user. Because sites are power-limited it measures how much revenue a datacenter can produce.
NVIDIA's open-source family of tools for building and adapting AI models: data curation, training and fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, evaluation and guardrails.
An open-source NVIDIA toolkit that adds programmable rules around a language model's inputs and outputs, for example blocking off-topic answers or enforcing a dialogue flow.
NVIDIA's family of open-weight AI models, released with much of their training data and recipes. The 2025-26 Nemotron 3 models are sparse hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts designs.

A neural-network layer that carries a fixed-size running state through a sequence instead of attending to every earlier token, so its memory does not grow with context length. Used alongside attention in hybrid models.
NVIDIA's reference applications (for example a research agent or a retrieval pipeline) built from NIM microservices and NeMo tools, published as starting code for enterprises.
The largest public hub for sharing AI models, datasets and demos, and the maker of widely used open-source model libraries. NVIDIA agreed in 2026 to acquire it (pending regulatory review).
